pacman::p_load(shiny, ggplot2, bslib, dplyr, tidyr, waiter) # 1. Define the UI ui <- page_navbar( title = "It Depends", theme = bs_theme(version = 5, bootswatch = "flatly", primary = "#2c3e50"), fillable = FALSE, # single global scrollbar #adding waiter while page load header = tagList( tags$head( # dino cursor follower tags$style(HTML(" #cursor-follower { position: absolute; pointer-events: none; font-size: 40px; z-index: 9999; transition: top 0.05s, left 0.05s; } ")), tags$script(HTML(" $(document).ready(function() { $(document).mousemove(function(e) { $('#cursor-follower').css({ left: e.pageX + 15 + 'px', top: e.pageY - 15 + 'px' }); }); }); ")) ), div(id = "cursor-follower", "🦖") ), # ========================================== # TAB 1: CONFOUNDING BIAS # ========================================== nav_panel("Confounding", navset_card_underline( title = "Confounding bias", # -- SUB-TAB 1: Confounding example -- nav_panel("Confounding example", layout_columns(col_widths = c(4, 8), card( card_header(class = "bg-primary text-white", "What is a Confounder?"), card_body( HTML("
A Confounder needs to fulfill 3 criterea:
  1. It is associated with the Exposure.
  2. It is an independent cause, risk factor, or protective factor of the Outcome.
  3. It is not a mediator (not on the causal pathway) between them.
Smoking (Confounder)
↙         ↘
Coffee (Exp)       Heart Disease (Out)
"), p("It is showing how failing to adjust for smoking creates a massive spurious Odds Ratio between coffee and heart disease."), div(class = "bg-light p-3 rounded border", checkboxInput("conf_adjust", strong("Stratify Data (Adjust for Smoking)"), value = FALSE) ), hr(), h5("Analysis Insight:"), uiOutput("conf_verdict"), hr(), HTML("

*Note: This is a fictional dataset simulated for educational purposes. Inspired by classic examples in Gordis Epidemiology (6th Ed).

") ) ), card( fillable = FALSE, card_header("2x2 Tables & Mathematical Adjustment"), card_body( uiOutput("conf_tables"), hr(), plotOutput("plot_confounding", height = "400px") ) ) ) ), # -- SUB-TAB 2: Risk of Overadjustment-- nav_panel("Risk of Overadjustment", tags$head( tags$style(HTML(" .sim-container { background-color: #ffffff; max-width: 700px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 20px; border-radius: 10px; } .diagram { position: relative; height: 250px; margin: 40px 0; background: #f8fbff; border: 2px solid #e0e6ed; border-radius: 8px; } .node { position: absolute; padding: 15px 20px; background: #34495e; color: white; border-radius: 8px; font-weight: bold; text-align: center; z-index: 2; } #node-bmi { top: 100px; left: 20px; } #node-bp { top: 20px; left: 250px; background: #e74c3c; } #node-esrd { top: 100px; right: 20px; } .sim-svg { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; z-index: 1; } .sim-line { stroke: #2c3e50; stroke-width: 4; transition: all 0.4s ease; } .sim-arrow { fill: #2c3e50; transition: all 0.4s ease; } .blocked-path { stroke: #bdc3c7; stroke-dasharray: 5, 5; } .blocked-arrow { fill: #bdc3c7; } .block-x { position: absolute; top: 50px; left: 280px; font-size: 40px; color: #c0392b; font-weight: bold; z-index: 3; } .controls-box { text-align: center; margin: 20px 0; padding: 20px; background: #ecf0f1; border-radius: 8px; } .stats-box { display: flex; justify-content: space-around; padding: 20px; font-size: 1.2em; border-top: 2px solid #eee; } .stat-box { text-align: center; } .stat-value { font-size: 1.8em; font-weight: bold; display: block; margin-top: 5px; transition: color 0.3s; } ")) ), layout_columns(col_widths = c(12), card( card_header(class = "bg-primary text-white", "Direct vs. Indirect Pathways (BMI -> BP -> ESRD)"), card_body( div(class = "sim-container", div(class = "controls-box", checkboxInput("adjustToggle", tags$b("Apply Statistical Adjustment for Blood Pressure", style="color: #c0392b; font-size: 1.1em;"), value = FALSE), p("Watch how the model changes when we mathematically 'control' for the mediator.", style = "color: #555; margin-top: 5px;") ), uiOutput("diagramUI"), uiOutput("statsUI") ) ) ) ) ) ) ), # ========================================== # TAB 2: BERKSON'S PARADOX & SELECTION BIAS # ========================================== nav_panel("Berkson's / Selection Bias", navset_card_underline( title = "Selection Bias Scenarios", # -- SUB-TAB 1: Smoking & Melanoma (Flipped OR) -- nav_panel("Scenario 1: Flipped OR (Smoking & Melanoma)", layout_columns(col_widths = c(4, 8), card( card_header(class = "bg-primary text-white", "Smoking vs. Melanoma"), card_body( p("Smoking does not cause melanoma (True OR = 1.0). But smoking causes COPD and heart attacks, which drive hospital admissions. Watch how hospital controls artificially make smoking look protective."), hr(), div(class = "bg-light p-3 rounded border", sliderInput("s1_smoke_rate", "General Public Smoking Rate (%):", min = 5, max = 50, value = 20, step = 5), sliderInput("s1_hosp_smoke", "Admission Rate for Smokers (due to COPD, etc) (%):", min = 10, max = 80, value = 60, step = 5), sliderInput("s1_hosp_non", "Admission Rate for Non-Smokers (%):", min = 5, max = 30, value = 10, step = 5) ), hr(), h5("Epidemiological Impact:"), uiOutput("s1_dynamic_text"), hr(), HTML("

*Note: Fictional simulation demonstrating Berkson's Bias.

") ) ), card( fillable = FALSE, card_header("Study Data & Learning Details"), card_body( uiOutput("s1_tables"), hr(), plotOutput("plot_s1", height = "350px"), hr(), accordion( accordion_panel("The Logic (Artificial Inflation)", HTML("

When you select hospital controls, you are sampling people admitted for 'other diseases'. Because smoking is a massive driver of 'other diseases' (like heart attacks), your hospital control group is packed with smokers.

When comparing normal melanoma cases to a control group that is 60% smokers, the math spits out a spurious negative association, making smoking look protective.

")) ) ) ) ) ), # -- SUB-TAB 2: Coffee & Pancreatic Cancer (Heightened OR) -- nav_panel("Scenario 2: Heightened OR (Coffee & Cancer)", layout_columns(col_widths = c(4, 8), card( card_header(class = "bg-primary text-white", "Coffee vs. Pancreatic Cancer"), card_body( p("Coffee does not cause pancreatic cancer (True OR = 1.0). In 1981, researchers used GI ulcer patients as hospital controls. Because ulcer patients avoid coffee, watch how the risk is artificially inflated."), hr(), div(class = "bg-light p-3 rounded border", sliderInput("s2_coffee_norm", "Coffee Drinking in General Public (%):", min = 30, max = 90, value = 60, step = 5), sliderInput("s2_coffee_ulcer", "Coffee Drinking in Ulcer Patients (Controls) (%):", min = 0, max = 50, value = 10, step = 5), sliderInput("s2_hosp_ulcer", "Hospitalization Rate for Ulcers (%):", min = 10, max = 90, value = 80, step = 5) ), hr(), h5("Epidemiological Impact:"), uiOutput("s2_dynamic_text"), hr(), HTML("

*Note: Simulation based on the historical design flaw in MacMahon et al. (NEJM 1981).

") ) ), card( fillable = FALSE, card_header("Study Data & Learning Details"), card_body( uiOutput("s2_tables"), hr(), plotOutput("plot_s2", height = "350px"), hr(), accordion( accordion_panel("The Logic (Artificial Deflation)", HTML("

This mimics the infamous 1981 MacMahon study. The researchers used gastrointestinal (GI) clinic patients as controls. GI ulcer patients actively avoid coffee because it hurts their stomachs.

By comparing normal cancer cases (who drink regular amounts of coffee) to a control group that drinks almost no coffee, the cases looked like extreme addicts. This created a spurious positive association, falsely labeling coffee as a carcinogen.

")) ) ) ) ) ), # -- SUB-TAB 3: Low Birth Weight (Continuous Collider) -- nav_panel("Scenario 3: Low Birth Weight (LBW)", layout_columns(col_widths = c(4, 8), card( card_header(class = "bg-primary text-white", "The Maternal Smoking Paradox"), card_body( HTML("
Analysis Goal:

We are analyzing whether Maternal Smoking (Exposure) increases the risk of Lethal Genetic Defects (Outcome).

In reality, they are completely independent. However, both smoking and genetic defects independently cause a baby to be born small (Low Birth Weight). Watch what happens when we filter our analysis to look ONLY at LBW babies.

"), div(class = "bg-light p-3 rounded border", checkboxInput("lbw_filter", strong("Condition on Collider (View ONLY LBW Babies)"), value = FALSE) ), hr(), h5("Analysis View:"), uiOutput("lbw_dynamic_text"), hr(), HTML("

*Note: Fictional simulation demonstrating the LBW Collider Paradox (Rothman, Modern Epidemiology).

") ) ), card( fillable = FALSE, card_header("Scatter Plot: Smoking vs. Lethal Risk"), card_body( plotOutput("plot_lbw", height = "450px"), hr(), accordion( accordion_panel("Why does this happen?", HTML("

If a mother did not smoke, but her baby is still Low Birth Weight, the baby must have a severe unmeasured condition (like a devastating genetic defect) to explain the small size.

By filtering to only LBW babies, we accidentally compare 'otherwise healthy babies of smokers' to 'severely ill babies of non-smokers'. This forces a spurious negative correlation, creating the dangerous illusion that smoking protects against lethal defects.

")) ) ) ) ) ) ) ), # ========================================== # TAB 3: COLLIDER BIAS # ========================================== nav_panel("Collider Bias", layout_columns(col_widths = c(4, 8), card( card_header(class = "bg-primary text-white", "What is a Collider?"), card_body( HTML("
The Core Rule:

A Collider is a variable that is caused by two other independent variables. If you condition your analysis on a collider (e.g., filtering your dataset), you open a backdoor path and force a spurious correlation between the two original variables.

Talent (Var A)         Looks (Var B)
↘                 ↙
Actor Status (Collider)
"), p("Talent and looks have zero correlation at birth. Watch what happens when we only analyze successful actors."), div(class = "bg-light p-3 rounded border", checkboxInput("col_adjust", strong("Condition on Collider (View Actors Only)"), value = FALSE) ), hr(), h5("Analysis View:"), uiOutput("col_dynamic_text"), hr(), HTML("

*Note: Fictional dataset simulating M-bias / Collider bias.

") ) ), card(card_body(fillable = FALSE, plotOutput("plot_collider", height = "550px"))) ) ), # ========================================== # TAB 4: MEASUREMENT ERROR # ========================================== nav_panel("Measurement Error", layout_columns(col_widths = c(4, 8), card( card_header(class = "bg-primary text-white", "Attenuation to the Null"), card_body( h4("Blood Pressure vs. Stroke Risk"), p("Real-world data collection is rarely perfect. 'Clinical measurement noise' refers to random errors, such as a slightly loose blood pressure cuff, a nervous patient, or a nurse rounding the numbers."), p("Watch how this random noise spreads the data out and hides the true strength of the causal relationship."), hr(), div(class = "bg-light p-3 rounded border", sliderInput("meas_error", strong("Clinical Measurement Error (Noise/Random Error):"), min = 0, max = 40, value = 0, step = 5) ), hr(), h5("Analysis View:"), uiOutput("meas_dynamic_text"), hr(), HTML("

*Note: Fictional simulation of non-differential measurement error.

") ) ), card(card_body(fillable = FALSE, plotOutput("plot_measurement", height = "550px"))) ) ) ) # --------------------------------------------------------- # 2. Define the Server Logic # --------------------------------------------------------- server <- function(input, output) { # ========================================== # TAB 1: CONFOUNDING BIAS # ========================================== conf_data <- reactive({ smokers <- data.frame( Smoking = rep("Smoker", 3000), Coffee = c(rep("Heavy Drinker", 2700), rep("Low/None", 300)), HeartDisease = c(rep("Case", 540), rep("Control", 2160), rep("Case", 60), rep("Control", 240)) ) non_smokers <- data.frame( Smoking = rep("Non-Smoker", 7000), Coffee = c(rep("Heavy Drinker", 700), rep("Low/None", 6300)), HeartDisease = c(rep("Case", 35), rep("Control", 665), rep("Case", 315), rep("Control", 5985)) ) df <- rbind(smokers, non_smokers) df$Coffee <- factor(df$Coffee, levels = c("Heavy Drinker", "Low/None")) df$HeartDisease <- factor(df$HeartDisease, levels = c("Case", "Control")) df }) conf_calc <- reactive({ df <- conf_data() calc_metrics <- function(data) { tbl <- table(data$Coffee, data$HeartDisease) a <- tbl[1,1]; b <- tbl[1,2] c <- tbl[2,1]; d <- tbl[2,2] or <- (a * d) / (b * c) risk_exp <- a / (a + b) risk_unexp <- c / (c + d) list(tbl = tbl, a=a, b=b, c=c, d=d, or=or, r_exp=risk_exp, r_unexp=risk_unexp) } list( crude = calc_metrics(df), smokers = calc_metrics(subset(df, Smoking == "Smoker")), non = calc_metrics(subset(df, Smoking == "Non-Smoker")) ) }) output$conf_verdict <- renderUI({ res <- conf_calc() if (input$conf_adjust) { HTML(paste0("
CONFOUNDING REVEALED
Once we stratify by smoking status, the association disappears entirely. The True Stratified OR is exactly ", round(res$smokers$or, 2), ". Coffee is innocent!
")) } else { HTML(paste0("
SPURIOUS ASSOCIATION
Looking at the naive data, coffee appears highly dangerous with a Crude OR of ", round(res$crude$or, 2), ". This is because coffee drinkers are heavily skewed toward being smokers.
")) } }) output$conf_tables <- renderUI({ res <- conf_calc() build_html_table <- function(title, m, color_class) { HTML(paste0( "
", title, "
", "", "", "", "", "", "
CaseControlTotalRisk (Case/Total)
Exp (Heavy)", m$a, "", m$b, "", m$a + m$b, "", round(m$r_exp * 100, 1), "%
Unexp (Low)", m$c, "", m$d, "", m$c + m$d, "", round(m$r_unexp * 100, 1), "%
Total", m$a + m$c, "", m$b + m$d, "", m$a+m$b+m$c+m$d, "
", "

Legend: a=Exp Case, b=Exp Ctrl, c=Unexp Case, d=Unexp Ctrl

", "

Odds Ratio = (a × d) / (b × c)
", "(", m$a, " × ", m$d, ") / (", m$b, " × ", m$c, ") = ", round(m$or, 2), "

" )) } if (!input$conf_adjust) { build_html_table("CRUDE ANALYSIS (Unadjusted)", res$crude, "text-danger") } else { HTML(paste0( "
", "
", build_html_table("STRATUM 1: SMOKERS", res$smokers, "text-success"), "
", "
", build_html_table("STRATUM 2: NON-SMOKERS", res$non, "text-success"), "
", "
" )) } }) output$plot_confounding <- renderPlot({ df <- conf_data() if (!input$conf_adjust) { plot_df <- df %>% count(Coffee, HeartDisease) %>% group_by(Coffee) %>% mutate(Risk = n / sum(n)) %>% filter(HeartDisease == "Case") ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Coffee, y = Risk, fill = Coffee)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.5, color="black") + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Heavy Drinker" = "#e74c3c", "Low/None" = "#bdc3c7")) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 0.25)) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + labs(title = "Crude Heart Disease Risk (Unadjusted)", y = "Absolute Risk (%)", x = "Coffee Consumption") + theme(legend.position = "none") } else { plot_df <- df %>% count(Smoking, Coffee, HeartDisease) %>% group_by(Smoking, Coffee) %>% mutate(Risk = n / sum(n)) %>% filter(HeartDisease == "Case") ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Coffee, y = Risk, fill = Coffee)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", color="black", width = 0.6) + facet_wrap(~Smoking) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Heavy Drinker" = "#3498db", "Low/None" = "#95a5a6")) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 0.25)) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + labs(title = "Stratified Heart Disease Risk (Adjusted for Smoking)", y = "Absolute Risk (%)", x = "Coffee Consumption") + theme(legend.position = "none", strip.background = element_rect(fill="#2c3e50", color=NA), strip.text = element_text(color="white", face="bold")) } }) # ========================================== # TAB 1 - SUB-TAB 2: OVERADJUSTMENT # ========================================== output$diagramUI <- renderUI({ is_adj <- input$adjustToggle path_class <- ifelse(is_adj, "sim-line blocked-path", "sim-line") arrow_class <- ifelse(is_adj, "blocked-arrow", "sim-arrow") HTML(paste0('
', ifelse(is_adj, '
✖
', ''), '
Exposure
(BMI)
Mediator
(Blood Pressure)
Outcome
(ESRD)
')) }) output$statsUI <- renderUI({ is_adj <- input$adjustToggle state_text <- ifelse(is_adj, "Adjusted (Blocked)", "Unadjusted (Total)") state_color <- ifelse(is_adj, "#c0392b", "#27ae60") rr_value <- ifelse(is_adj, "4.68", "6.12") HTML(paste0('
Model State: ', state_text, '
Observed Relative Risk: ', rr_value, '
')) }) # ========================================== # TAB 2 - SCENARIO 1: SMOKING & MELANOMA # ========================================== s1_data <- reactive({ set.seed(111) n <- 20000 p_smoke <- input$s1_smoke_rate / 100 smoking <- rbinom(n, 1, p_smoke) melanoma <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.05) p_hosp_smoke <- input$s1_hosp_smoke / 100 p_hosp_non <- input$s1_hosp_non / 100 prob_hosp <- ifelse(melanoma == 1, 1.0, ifelse(smoking == 1, p_hosp_smoke, p_hosp_non)) hospitalized <- rbinom(n, 1, prob_hosp) data.frame( Smoking = factor(smoking, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Smoker", "Non-Smoker")), Melanoma = factor(melanoma, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Case", "Control")), Hospitalized = factor(hospitalized, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Hospital", "Community")) ) }) s1_calc <- reactive({ df <- s1_data() tbl_comm <- table(df$Smoking, df$Melanoma) or_comm <- (tbl_comm[1,1] * tbl_comm[2,2]) / (tbl_comm[1,2] * tbl_comm[2,1]) df_hosp <- subset(df, Hospitalized == "Hospital") tbl_hosp <- table(df_hosp$Smoking, df_hosp$Melanoma) or_hosp <- (tbl_hosp[1,1] * tbl_hosp[2,2]) / (tbl_hosp[1,2] * tbl_hosp[2,1]) list(tbl_comm = tbl_comm, tbl_hosp = tbl_hosp, or_comm = or_comm, or_hosp = or_hosp) }) output$s1_dynamic_text <- renderUI({ res <- s1_calc() HTML(paste0( "
Community True OR: ", round(res$or_comm, 2), " (Independent)
", "
Hospital Sample OR: ", round(res$or_hosp, 2), " (Spurious Protective)
" )) }) output$s1_tables <- renderUI({ res <- s1_calc() HTML(paste0( "
", "
Community (True Truth)
", "", "", "", "", "
Case (a/c)Control (b/d)
Smoker (Exp)", res$tbl_comm[1,1], "", res$tbl_comm[1,2], "
Non (Unexp)", res$tbl_comm[2,1], "", res$tbl_comm[2,2], "
", "
Hospital (Biased)
", "", "", "", "", "
Case (a/c)Control (b/d)
Smoker (Exp)", res$tbl_hosp[1,1], "", res$tbl_hosp[1,2], "
Non (Unexp)", res$tbl_hosp[2,1], "", res$tbl_hosp[2,2], "
" )) }) output$plot_s1 <- renderPlot({ df <- s1_data() plot_df <- df %>% count(Hospitalized, Melanoma, Smoking) %>% group_by(Hospitalized, Melanoma) %>% mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Melanoma, y = prop, fill = Smoking)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", color="black", linewidth=0.2) + facet_wrap(~Hospitalized) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Smoker" = "#e74c3c", "Non-Smoker" = "#ecf0f1")) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + labs(title = "Smoking Rate in Melanoma Cases vs Controls", y = "% Smokers", x = "") + theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_rect(fill="#34495e", color=NA), strip.text = element_text(color="white", face="bold")) }) # ========================================== # TAB 2 - SCENARIO 2: COFFEE & CANCER # ========================================== s2_data <- reactive({ set.seed(222) n <- 20000 cancer <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.02) ulcer <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.10) p_norm <- input$s2_coffee_norm / 100 p_ulcer <- input$s2_coffee_ulcer / 100 coffee <- ifelse(ulcer == 1, rbinom(n, 1, p_ulcer), rbinom(n, 1, p_norm)) p_hosp_ulcer <- input$s2_hosp_ulcer / 100 prob_hosp <- ifelse(cancer == 1, 1.0, ifelse(ulcer == 1, p_hosp_ulcer, 0.05)) hospitalized <- rbinom(n, 1, prob_hosp) data.frame(Coffee = factor(coffee, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Drinker", "Non-Drinker")), Cancer = factor(cancer, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Case", "Control")), Hospitalized = factor(hospitalized, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Hospital", "Community"))) }) s2_calc <- reactive({ df <- s2_data() tbl_comm <- table(df$Coffee, df$Cancer) or_comm <- (tbl_comm[1,1] * tbl_comm[2,2]) / (tbl_comm[1,2] * tbl_comm[2,1]) df_hosp <- subset(df, Hospitalized == "Hospital") tbl_hosp <- table(df_hosp$Coffee, df_hosp$Cancer) or_hosp <- (tbl_hosp[1,1] * tbl_hosp[2,2]) / (tbl_hosp[1,2] * tbl_hosp[2,1]) list(tbl_comm = tbl_comm, tbl_hosp = tbl_hosp, or_comm = or_comm, or_hosp = or_hosp) }) output$s2_dynamic_text <- renderUI({ res <- s2_calc() HTML(paste0( "
Community True OR: ", round(res$or_comm, 2), " (Independent)
", "
Hospital Sample OR: ", round(res$or_hosp, 2), " (Spurious Harmful)
" )) }) output$s2_tables <- renderUI({ res <- s2_calc() HTML(paste0( "
", "
Community (True Truth)
", "", "", "", "", "
Case (a/c)Control (b/d)
Coffee (Exp)", res$tbl_comm[1,1], "", res$tbl_comm[1,2], "
Non (Unexp)", res$tbl_comm[2,1], "", res$tbl_comm[2,2], "
", "
Hospital (Biased)
", "", "", "", "", "
Case (a/c)Control (b/d)
Coffee (Exp)", res$tbl_hosp[1,1], "", res$tbl_hosp[1,2], "
Non (Unexp)", res$tbl_hosp[2,1], "", res$tbl_hosp[2,2], "
" )) }) output$plot_s2 <- renderPlot({ df <- s2_data() plot_df <- df %>% count(Hospitalized, Cancer, Coffee) %>% group_by(Hospitalized, Cancer) %>% mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Cancer, y = prop, fill = Coffee)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", color="black", linewidth=0.2) + facet_wrap(~Hospitalized) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Drinker" = "#8e44ad", "Non-Drinker" = "#ecf0f1")) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + labs(title = "Coffee Drinking in Cancer Cases vs Controls", y = "% Coffee Drinkers", x = "") + theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_rect(fill="#34495e", color=NA), strip.text = element_text(color="white", face="bold")) }) # ========================================== # TAB 2 - SCENARIO 3: LOW BIRTH WEIGHT # ========================================== lbw_data <- reactive({ set.seed(888) n <- 1000 smoking <- runif(n, 0, 20) lethal_defect <- rnorm(n, 50, 15) birth_weight <- 3800 - (30 * smoking) - (15 * lethal_defect) + rnorm(n, 0, 200) is_lbw <- ifelse(birth_weight < 2500, "Low Birth Weight (<2.5kg)", "Normal Weight") data.frame(smoking, lethal_defect, birth_weight, is_lbw) }) output$lbw_dynamic_text <- renderUI({ df <- lbw_data() if (input$lbw_filter) { df_lbw <- subset(df, is_lbw == "Low Birth Weight (<2.5kg)") r_lbw <- cor(df_lbw$smoking, df_lbw$lethal_defect) HTML(paste0("
SPURIOUS NEGATIVE CORRELATION
LBW Babies Only (r = ", round(r_lbw, 2), ")

Among small babies, higher smoking correlates with lower severe genetic risk. This falsely suggests smoking protects against lethal defects!
")) } else { r_gen <- cor(df$smoking, df$lethal_defect) HTML(paste0("
TRUE INDEPENDENCE
All Births (r = ", round(r_gen, 2), ")

In the total population, a mother's smoking status has no relation to random genetic defects.
")) } }) output$plot_lbw <- renderPlot({ df <- lbw_data() p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = smoking, y = lethal_defect)) + theme_minimal(base_size = 15) + labs(x = "Maternal Smoking (Cigarettes/Day)", y = "Unmeasured Lethal Defect (Severity)") + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 20), ylim = c(0, 100)) if (input$lbw_filter) { ggplot(subset(df, is_lbw == "Low Birth Weight (<2.5kg)"), aes(x = smoking, y = lethal_defect)) + geom_point(color = "#e74c3c", size = 3, alpha = 0.7) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#c0392b", linewidth = 1.5) + theme_minimal(base_size = 15) + labs(x = "Maternal Smoking (Cigarettes/Day)", y = "Unmeasured Lethal Defect (Severity)", title = "View: ONLY Low Birth Weight Babies") + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 20), ylim = c(0, 100)) } else { p + geom_point(aes(color = is_lbw), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#2c3e50", linewidth = 1.5) + scale_color_manual(values = c("Low Birth Weight (<2.5kg)" = "#e74c3c", "Normal Weight" = "#bdc3c7")) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank()) + labs(title = "View: All Babies (General Population)") } }) # ========================================== # TAB 3: COLLIDER BIAS # ========================================== set.seed(99) df_col <- data.frame(talent = rnorm(1000, 50, 15), looks = rnorm(1000, 50, 15)) df_col$is_actor <- ifelse((df_col$talent + df_col$looks) > 130, "Actor", "General Public") output$col_dynamic_text <- renderUI({ if (input$col_adjust) { r_actor <- cor(subset(df_col, is_actor == "Actor")$talent, subset(df_col, is_actor == "Actor")$looks) HTML(paste0("
SPURIOUS CORRELATION
Actors Only (r = ", round(r_actor, 2), ")

Conditioning on a collider (Actor status) forces the traits to become negatively correlated.
")) } else { r_gen <- cor(df_col$talent, df_col$looks) HTML(paste0("
TRUE INDEPENDENCE
General Population (r = ", round(r_gen, 2), ")

At birth, talent and looks are completely independent.
")) } }) output$plot_collider <- renderPlot({ p <- ggplot(df_col, aes(x = talent, y = looks)) + theme_minimal(base_size = 16) + labs(x = "Acting Talent", y = "Physical Attractiveness") + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100)) if (input$col_adjust) { ggplot(subset(df_col, is_actor == "Actor"), aes(x = talent, y = looks)) + geom_point(color = "#f39c12", size = 3, alpha = 0.8) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#d35400", linewidth = 1.5) + theme_minimal(base_size = 16) + labs(x = "Acting Talent", y = "Physical Attractiveness") + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100)) } else { p + geom_point(color = "#95a5a6", size = 3, alpha = 0.5) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#2c3e50", linewidth = 1.5) } }) # ========================================== # TAB 4: MEASUREMENT ERROR # ========================================== meas_data <- reactive({ set.seed(101) true_bp <- rnorm(500, 120, 15) true_risk <- 0.5 * true_bp + rnorm(500, 0, 10) measured_bp <- true_bp + rnorm(500, 0, input$meas_error) data.frame(measured_bp, true_risk) }) output$meas_dynamic_text <- renderUI({ df <- meas_data() model <- lm(true_risk ~ measured_bp, data = df) slope <- coef(model)[2] if (input$meas_error == 0) { HTML(paste0("
PERFECT MEASUREMENT
Observed Effect: +", round(slope, 2), "

With a perfect blood pressure cuff, we see the true steep causal relationship.
")) } else { HTML(paste0("
ATTENUATED EFFECT
Observed Effect: +", round(slope, 2), "

As noise increases, the slope flattens out (attenuates toward the null).
")) } }) output$plot_measurement <- renderPlot({ df <- meas_data() ggplot(df, aes(x = measured_bp, y = true_risk)) + geom_point(color = "#9b59b6", size = 3, alpha = 0.6) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#2c3e50", linewidth = 1.5) + theme_minimal(base_size = 16) + labs(x = "Measured Blood Pressure (with error)", y = "Stroke Risk Score") + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(60, 180), ylim = c(20, 100)) }) } shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

name: README.md
content:
# It-Depends

This project is built for educational purposes only. The intention is to create an interactive web app (built with R Shiny) where students can visualize and simulate complex epidemiological biases during their learning.

There are many possible biases in epidemiological studies, and the same type of bias is often referred to by different names. While this tool does not exhaustively cover every potential bias, the visualizations and simulations have been curated to present the biases commonly discussed in the field.

This project is open to further enrichment, including but not limited to new content, varied examples, innovative visualizations, and UI/UX improvements. 

**Disclaimer:** The code for this interactive web tool was written using Google Gemini based on the author's epidemiological specifications.
